quotes.text: He is the father of three teenage boys and enjoys cycling in his (limited) spare time!
Dr Tal Jacobson is kind and approachable with an easy going and relaxed manner that will put you at ease.
Dr Jacobson is a skilled specialist practitioner and an accomplished academic, with a career that has taken him around the world.
After completing his training in the UK, he spent a number of years practising in New Zealand before moving to Brisbane in 2010.
He teaches other doctors on a range of courses including anatomy, surgery and evidence based medicine.
He is professional, confidential and courteous.

As the Director of Eve Health, Dr Jacobson is able to offer his patients a highly personalised service, with the back-up of on-call obstetricians, as well as onsite midwives, physiotherapists, psychologists, dieticians and nurses.
Outside of obstetrics, Dr Jacobson and his wife have three teenage boys, a golden labrador and three cats who keep them busy.
He is also a keen road cyclist who often uses this interest to raise money for charities, by taking part in city-to-city charity rides.

personal.philosophy_of_care: Caring for people across their whole lifetime is an honour; midlife care needs attention to every aspect of a woman's health and life, which takes time that must be deliberately prioritised.

personal.communication_approach: Takes time; whole-of-life, comprehensive view of midlife health.

personal.outside_medicine: Family, friends and her golden retriever are her idea of bliss.

quotes.text: In her free time, Dr McCormack is learning French and enjoys participating in middle to long-distance trail and road races, as well as strength training.
She finds solace in her kitchen through cooking and singing musicals as if no one is listening. Being with her family, friends, and her golden retriever is her idea of bliss.
Dr McCormack feels it is an honour to care for individuals throughout their lifetime, offering support and engagement during health challenges.
Her decision to specialise in general practice was driven by a desire to provide comprehensive care to her patients at every stage of life.
One of the main challenges in providing this care is ensuring attention to all aspects of a woman's health and life, as each plays a vital role in overall well-being.
This comprehensive approach requires time, which may not always be readily available in healthcare settings unless it is prioritised as essential for midlife care.
Her training in General Practice took place in Cairns, and she started practicing as a GP in Brisbane in 2007.
Throughout her career, she has remained dedicated to general practice, caring for patients of all ages, while also nurturing her passion for women's health and sexual health in a specialised setting.
